industry_analogy: Insurance claims touch-reason coding; contact-centre reason codes (svc.md §7)
why_no_predecessor: RR-REQ-X-048-r2 types WHY a WorkItem may be created (causes a–e) and UNB-RCN-PLT-006 asks each rule to state the decision only a human can make, but neither types the human-intervention class on the item, so avoidable administrative work cannot be separated from legally required judgment in metrics or prevention.
business_problem: Every recurring human task is an operating expense. Without a typed reason for each human touch, the enterprise cannot tell which touches are mandatory (law, fiduciary duty, independent control) and which are root-cause opportunities, and AI involvement tends to be used as a blanket reason for review.
statement: Every WorkItem, human approval task and human touch recorded against an outcome MUST carry exactly one primary HumanInterventionClass from the versioned taxonomy {LegallyRequiredJudgment, FiduciaryGovernance, IndependentControl, MaterialFinancialRisk, AmbiguousEvidence, NovelCircumstance, CustomerRequestedAssistance, SystemFailure, AvoidableAdministrative}, assigned deterministically by the creating rule (not by the assignee), plus the rule id and the authority-matrix action class (UNB-RCN-PLT-005). 'AI involvement', 'AI confidence' or 'AI-generated' MUST NOT be a class or a sufficient creating condition; a rule that routes AI output to a human MUST cite one of the nine classes (normally AmbiguousEvidence or NovelCircumstance) with the evidence condition. A creating rule whose items are classed AvoidableAdministrative MUST declare a prevention owner; when such a rule produces more than the configured volume (default 25 items) in each of two consecutive periods, the platform MUST open a REQ-X-042 InterventionProposal. Reporting MUST show human touches per 1,000 outcomes by class, rule and sponsor.
applicability: All sponsors, all case kinds, all operating models (REQ-X-057).
rationale: Makes the mission principle 'every exception is a root-cause opportunity' measurable and prevents AI review creep without weakening reserved human authority.

acceptance_criteria.given: a deterministic rule creates a WorkItem for a sanctions potential match
acceptance_criteria.then: its class is IndependentControl or LegallyRequiredJudgment as declared on the rule, the rule id and action class are recorded, and the assignee cannot change the class

acceptance_criteria.given: a rule definition whose only creating condition is 'AI recommendation present' or 'AI confidence < x'
acceptance_criteria.when: the rule is validated for publication
acceptance_criteria.then: publication fails with HIC_AI_INVOLVEMENT_NOT_A_CLASS

acceptance_criteria.given: a rule classed AvoidableAdministrative created 40 items in each of two consecutive months (threshold 25)
acceptance_criteria.then: an InterventionProposal is opened against the rule's prevention owner and appears on the operating-metrics view

acceptance_criteria.given: an item without a class
acceptance_criteria.then: the command is rejected HIC_CLASS_REQUIRED and no item is created

failure_conditions: Class missing or editable by assignee
AI involvement used as review trigger
Avoidable-administrative volume grows without a proposal
security_compliance: Class is part of the audit record; restricted-investigation items keep their access class (UNB-XIN-CLM-004).
ai_automation: Deterministic assignment of class by rule. AI may propose a class for new rule drafts; it cannot set the class on items.
ui_implications: Work item header shows class and why a human is needed in plain language; filters by class.
api_implications: WorkItem resource exposes humanInterventionClass, creatingRuleId, actionClass; error codes HIC_CLASS_REQUIRED, HIC_AI_INVOLVEMENT_NOT_A_CLASS.
reporting_implications: Human touches per 1,000 outcomes by class/rule/sponsor; AvoidableAdministrative trend; per-kind reporting (no averaging across kinds).
testing_requirements: Rule-publication negative tests; property test that every created item has a class; metric fixture tests.
priority_justification: Cheap to add at the WorkItem kernel before volume exists; expensive to retrofit; directly drives staffing levers.
argue_for: Separates mandatory from avoidable work; blocks review creep from AI involvement; feeds prevention loop.
argue_against: Another mandatory field; classification disputes; nine classes may be too many for small sponsors.
existing_capability_alternative: RR-REQ-X-048-r2 creation causes plus UNB-RCN-PLT-006 free-text 'decision only a human can make' — insufficient because untyped and not per item.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Low: a field on the rule definition and the item; taxonomy governance owned by compliance.
simplest_valid_alternative: Class on the creating rule only, inherited by items (adopted: items inherit, cannot override).
decision_rationale: Adopt with rule-level assignment to avoid per-item classification labour.
open_questions: Should SystemFailure items be excluded from staffing forecasts (they are incident-driven)?
Threshold default 25 per period — calibrate in pilot.
accessibility_considerations: Class labels have plain-language descriptions readable by screen readers.
financial_implications: Enables attribution of labour cost by intervention class (UNB-XIN-ECO-006 time equations).
expected_behavior: Every human touch is typed; avoidable classes generate prevention proposals.
exception_behavior: Unclassifiable item → creation rejected and rule flagged; for safety the underlying outcome stays held (never auto-approved).

discovery_source: Phase Six staffing floor challenge (TVC-018, TVF-163)
industry_analogy: Bank dual-control rosters; hospital on-call coverage matrices
parent_capability: Minimum responsible staffing and SoD floors
why_no_predecessor: TVF-163 proposes 'TVR-OPS-004 rota' and organization §4 says 'A rota and on-call model is required (TVR-OPS-004)', but TVR-OPS-004 is never defined (undefined-references.csv:558). UNB-XIN-ECO-017 forecasts hours, not lawful-approver availability.
business_problem: A sponsor can have enough FTE on paper yet no lawful approver on a given day (holiday, illness, conflict), which either stops grants/payments or pressures staff to bypass segregation of duties.
statement: For each reserved decision class in the authority matrix (UNB-RCN-PLT-005) that has a service-level clock, the platform MUST compute daily, for the next 20 business days (configurable), an AuthorityCoverage record: the set of principals holding a valid DoA entry for that class (UNB-XIN-ERP-005) who are scheduled available, minus those excluded by recorded absence; and it MUST test whether the class's distinctness requirement can be met (e.g. two approvers excluding the releaser for NotReceived; payee approver ≠ releaser) using per-item SoD history rather than fixed role-per-person assignments. When coverage fails for any day, the platform MUST open a CoverageGap work item (class FiduciaryGovernance) for the accountable executive at least 10 business days before the day (or immediately if later), listing pre-authorized backup delegates that would close the gap. The platform MUST NOT relax SoD, auto-approve, or extend an approver's authority to close a gap; items that cannot be decided wait with their SLA status and customer notice per their profile.
applicability: All sponsors; mandatory before go-live for any sponsor whose DoA names fewer than 5 holders for a payment-chain class.
rationale: Converts the disputed '6–8' vs '~10' staffing floor into a checkable, per-sponsor invariant: named, available, distinct authority holders per class per day.

acceptance_criteria.given: 5 cross-trained treasury-authorized holders, 2 on leave Dec 24–Jan 2
acceptance_criteria.then: every class including NotReceived (two approvers excluding releaser) is satisfiable on each day and no gap is opened

acceptance_criteria.given: 3 of the 5 on leave Dec 29
acceptance_criteria.then: a CoverageGap item is created for Dec 29 naming the class NotReceived and listing pre-authorized backups; no SoD rule is changed

acceptance_criteria.given: a gap day arrives without resolution and a NotReceived item ages
acceptance_criteria.then: it escalates per its profile and remains undecided; no single approver can resolve it

acceptance_criteria.given: a DoA holder becomes inactive in the workforce feed
acceptance_criteria.then: the holder is excluded and any resulting gap is reported

failure_conditions: Coverage computed from role titles instead of DoA entries
Gap closed by relaxing SoD
Absences not reflected
security_compliance: Coverage data reveals staff schedules; restrict to accountable executive, finance authority and HR.
ui_implications: Coverage calendar per class with red days; gap work item shows candidate backups.
api_implications: Read-only AuthorityCoverage query; no command can alter SoD from this surface.
reporting_implications: Coverage gaps per period; days with single-point-of-failure classes.
testing_requirements: Fixtures for holiday rotas; property test that SoD constraints are never relaxed.
priority_justification: Holiday coverage failure is a severity-4 review finding (review-fin-ops B-2); cost is low.
argue_for: Makes the staffing floor explicit and testable per sponsor; avoids over-hiring to a generic number.
argue_against: Requires reliable absence data; small sponsors may resent scheduling overhead.
existing_capability_alternative: OPS-004 (named owner, backup, reviewer per control) covers controls, not decision classes or days.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Moderate: absence data integration; SoD history evaluation is shared with authorization engine.
simplest_valid_alternative: Monthly manual rota attested by accountable executive (rejected: does not detect sick-day gaps).
decision_rationale: Adopt; it defines the missing TVR-OPS-004 behaviour.
open_questions: Coverage depth (single vs double absence) is SPD-ORG-003.
Whether deterministic release counts as a releaser (SPD-ORG-001) changes the distinctness count.
financial_implications: Sets the staffing floor used by UNB-XIN-ECO-015 ratchet (RR-UNB-ECO-003-r1).
preconditions: DoA register and absence data available.
exception_behavior: Missing absence data → treat holder as available but flag coverage 'Unverified'; never as a pass for go-live.

discovery_source: ECN Phase Four cost-floor analysis (executed model)
industry_analogy: Bank cost-to-serve account fee justification (analogy; no citation)
why_no_predecessor: UNB-XIN-ECO-018 requires cost basis and recovery ratio only for service charges; UNB-XIN-ERP-001 computes minimum fees but requires no cost basis; UNB-XIN-ADV-001 budgets recurring obligations, not minimum fees.
business_problem: Minimum fees and minimum balances exclude small donors without evidence that the minimum reflects the cost of serving them.
statement: Each fee-schedule version that sets a minimum annual fee, a minimum opening balance or a minimum fund balance SHALL reference a CostBasis record for each servicing class it applies to, stating marginal variable cost per account-year, fully allocated cost per account-year (sponsor-level and fund-borne costs shown separately, never included), their confidence grade and P10/P50/P90 range, and the ratio of the minimum to the fully allocated P50. Publication of the schedule version SHALL be rejected when the CostBasis is missing or older than 13 months, or when the ratio exceeds a configured ceiling (default 1.5) unless an approver records a non-cost rationale category (cross-subsidy policy, distribution cost, risk) that is disclosed in the donor fee disclosure.
applicability: All sponsors and servicing classes with minimum fees or balances.
rationale: Model shows minimums of $100-$250 against lean fully allocated small-account cost of $17-50 and marginal cost of $5-24; minimums currently encode history and distribution.

acceptance_criteria.given: a schedule version with a $100 minimum for class Standard and a CostBasis showing fully allocated P50 $50 (grade C)
acceptance_criteria.when: the sponsor administrator publishes it without a rationale
acceptance_criteria.then: publication is rejected with MINIMUM_EXCEEDS_COST_CEILING showing ratio 2.0 and the ceiling 1.5

acceptance_criteria.given: the same schedule with rationale category 'cross-subsidy policy' recorded by an approver
acceptance_criteria.then: publication succeeds and the donor fee disclosure contains the rationale text

acceptance_criteria.given: a schedule version whose CostBasis is 14 months old
acceptance_criteria.then: it is rejected with COST_BASIS_STALE

acceptance_criteria.given: a CostBasis that includes sponsor-entity costs in the account-level figure
acceptance_criteria.then: validation fails with MIXED_COST_LEVELS

failure_conditions: minimum published with no CostBasis
fund-borne costs counted in sponsor cost basis
rationale not disclosed to donors
dependencies: UNB-XIN-ECO-004 reconciled attribution; UNB-XIN-ECO-007 metric registry
security_compliance: Fee reasonableness review (XID-ECO-002) and counsel review of disclosure; no donor-level profitability exposed (UNB-XIN-ECO-012).
ai_automation: Deterministic computation; AI may draft the rationale text only, approver signs.
ui_implications: Fee schedule editor shows ratio, grade and range; accessible text.
api_implications: FeeSchedule publish command validates CostBasis reference.
reporting_implications: Annual minimum-fee cost-basis report by class.
testing_requirements: Unit tests for ratio and staleness; scenario SPS-ECN-001.
priority_justification: Affects inclusion and fee reasonableness but not release-1 money movement.
argue_for: Turns an exclusionary price into an evidenced decision; aligns with ECO-018 cost-based pricing.
argue_against: Cost bases are grade C/D until measurement exists; may block legitimate minimums early.
customer_friction: None for donors; administrative for sponsors.
simplest_valid_alternative: Disclosure-only: publish the ratio without a ceiling.
decision_rationale: Ceiling with override keeps sponsor authority while forcing a recorded reason.
open_questions: Is 1.5 the right default ceiling?
Should minimum grant sizes (UNB-GRANT-045) be included?
accessibility_considerations: Ratio and grade conveyed as text, not colour.
financial_implications: May reduce minimum-fee revenue for small funds; offset via disclosed cross-subsidy.
preconditions: CostBasis computed from a ReconciliationRun within tolerance.

discovery_source: ECN Phase Five simulation (sudden_growth, major_sponsor_onboarding, major_migration scenarios)
industry_analogy: Admission control / capacity gating in contact centres and cloud capacity planning (analogy)
why_no_predecessor: UNB-XIN-ECO-017 forecasts capacity but forbids forecasts from gating anything and does not cover onboarding/migration decisions; UNB-XIN-ECO-016 counter-metrics apply to cost initiatives, not to growth.
business_problem: Onboarding a sponsor or migrating a book lowers cost per account while collapsing SLA attainment and leaving backlog unresolved.
statement: Before activating a sponsor onboarding, an inbound book migration or a growth campaign that adds more than a configured share (default 10%) of active accounts within any 60-business-day window, the platform SHALL run the capacity forecast (UNB-XIN-ECO-017) including the added steady-state volume and the declared one-off migration work, and SHALL require an approver acknowledgment recording the projected SLA attainment per queue, projected peak backlog and days to clear whenever any queue's projected SLA attainment is below its configured floor (default 90%) or projected backlog does not clear within 30 business days. Reductions in cost per account attributable to account growth SHALL be reported separately and SHALL NOT be credited as verified savings under UNB-XIN-ECO-015/019.
rationale: Executed model: major_migration at 100k reduces cost/acct while SLA falls to ~22% and >60k items remain unresolved 60 days after year-end.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/45711cf3-dc26-5c8e-a6da-4af8bd5f0946/scratchpad/simp/econ/results.json (executed: python3 -I -B model.py, seed 20261124) scenario_mc OM3|100000|major_migration, sudden_growth, major_sponsor_onboarding

acceptance_criteria.given: a migration adding 100% of current accounts with 0.15 ops cases and 0.5 contacts per migrated account
acceptance_criteria.then: the forecast runs, projected SLA attainment below 90% is shown per queue and activation requires an approver acknowledgment record

acceptance_criteria.given: an onboarding adding 5% of accounts
acceptance_criteria.then: no acknowledgment is required and the forecast is still logged

acceptance_criteria.given: a month where cost/acct fell 20% because accounts doubled
acceptance_criteria.then: the reduction appears under 'growth effect' and is not counted as a verified saving

acceptance_criteria.given: an acknowledged activation
acceptance_criteria.then: the record shows forecast version, inputs, approver and projected metrics

failure_conditions: activation without forecast
growth effect credited as saving
forecast used to defer or deny an individual grant
dependencies: UNB-XIN-ECO-017 capacity forecast; migration work declaration.
security_compliance: Forecast never gates legally required controls or individual grant processing; it gates activation scheduling only.
ui_implications: Activation screen shows projected SLA and backlog with accessible table.
api_implications: Activate-sponsor and start-migration commands require forecast id and, when below floor, acknowledgment id.
reporting_implications: Growth effect separated in economics pack.
priority_justification: Protects service during the highest-risk operational events; not needed for a single-sponsor R1.
argue_for: Prevents silent service collapse during growth; stops false efficiency claims.
argue_against: Adds a step to commercial onboarding; forecasts are grade C until measured.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Requires migration work estimates per account.
customer_friction: Possible later go-live dates for new sponsors.
decision_rationale: Acknowledgment, not block, preserves commercial authority while recording the trade-off.
open_questions: Default floor 90% vs contracted SLA tiers (UNB-XIN-ECO-020)?
exception_behavior: Emergency migration (sponsor failure) proceeds with post-hoc acknowledgment within 5 business days.
adversarial_disposition: fold into UNB-XIN-ECO-017 as an acceptance criterion (SPF-ADV-023)

discovery_source: ECN Phase Four theoretical cost floor (executed model)
why_no_predecessor: UNB-XIN-ADV-001 budgets only registered recurring obligations; it does not budget the class's expected human-touch, rail and AI cost, which the model shows dominate DigitalMinimal economics (ops returns, contacts). Revised statement of an UNB-XIN record is therefore proposed as a new linked requirement, not an RR.
business_problem: A DigitalMinimal program can pass the recurring-obligation budget and still be loss-making because expected contacts, returns and exceptions are unbudgeted.
statement: For each ServicingClass, the platform SHALL compute an expected marginal cost per account-year as the sum of (a) registered recurring-obligation cost (UNB-XIN-ADV-001), (b) expected payment-rail cost from the class's funding and grant rail mix, (c) expected human minutes (contacts, exceptions after determination reuse, ACH returns, reconciliation breaks) multiplied by the applicable capacity cost rate (UNB-XIN-ECO-006), and (d) expected AI and infrastructure unit costs, each with grade and P10/P50/P90. Publishing a DigitalMinimal program configuration SHALL be rejected when the expected marginal cost P50 exceeds the program's declared expected revenue per account-year (excluding fund-borne costs) unless a sponsor-approved subsidy source and amount are recorded. ServicingClass SHALL NOT be an input to eligibility, sanctions, approval, grant priority or payment timing.
applicability: Sponsors offering DigitalMinimal or workplace programs.
rationale: Executed model: workplace marginal cost ~$8-13/yr vs $9 revenue at 0.60% on $1.5k; ops queue largest labour pool in OM4.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/45711cf3-dc26-5c8e-a6da-4af8bd5f0946/scratchpad/simp/econ/results.json (executed: python3 -I -B model.py, seed 20261124) segment_economics OM4@1M, marginal_floor

acceptance_criteria.given: a DigitalMinimal workplace program with expected marginal cost P50 $13.10 and declared revenue $9.00 with no subsidy
acceptance_criteria.then: publication is rejected listing each cost component, grade and range

acceptance_criteria.given: the same program with an employer subsidy of $12 per account-year recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: publication succeeds and the subsidy is shown in the program economics view

acceptance_criteria.given: a DigitalMinimal and a Standard fund recommending grants to the same charity
acceptance_criteria.then: eligibility outcome and timing are identical and the decision trace shows ServicingClass was not read

acceptance_criteria.given: a component cost without grade
acceptance_criteria.when: the class cost model is saved
acceptance_criteria.then: save fails with MISSING_CONFIDENCE

failure_conditions: class cost used in any control decision
fund-borne costs counted as revenue offset
unbudgeted calendar obligations
dependencies: UNB-XIN-ADV-001 adopted; capacity cost rates measured.
security_compliance: Legal controls identical across classes; profitability not exposed to operations (UNB-XIN-ECO-012).
ui_implications: Program economics view with component table.
api_implications: Program publish validates class cost model.
reporting_implications: Class marginal cost vs revenue monthly.
priority_justification: Needed before any HVLB/workplace program (not R1 per 17-RELEASE-1-SCOPE).
argue_for: Prevents structurally loss-making programs; makes subsidies explicit.
argue_against: Grade C/D inputs until measured; could deter experimentation.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Needs per-class rail mix and contact-rate assumptions.
decision_rationale: Rejection with explicit subsidy override keeps the decision with the sponsor but forbids silent losses.
open_questions: Should employer subsidies be contractually committed before publish?
exception_behavior: Pilot flag allows publish for ≤1,000 accounts for 6 months with mandatory measurement.
adversarial_disposition: keep; add declared acquisition bearer and amount (SPF-ADV-006)

why_no_predecessor: AIN-007 is a principle; UNB-XIN-CLM-003 covers only information requests; UNB-UI-A-005 covers re-entry within one flow. No requirement registers customer interaction steps with a necessity basis or forbids pull-only wait states.
business_problem: Every unnecessary customer interaction is friction and a repeat-contact driver; no mechanism stops new ones being added.
statement: Unbound MUST maintain a versioned Interaction Register with one entry per customer-facing input, confirmation or wait step (donor, advisor, charity, sponsor officer, partner). Each entry MUST declare: persona, journey, data requested, necessity basis (law | consent | donor-control | security | convention) with citation, whether the data is already held or retrievable with authorization, inference or default rule, and the notification catalog event (UNB-RCN-PLT-002) that ends each wait step. A step with basis 'convention' MUST name an accountable owner and a review date. A wait step without a catalog event MUST NOT be released. A UI flow MUST NOT render an input whose register entry is absent.
applicability: All customer-facing surfaces, APIs used by embedded widgets, and staff-assisted flows that collect customer data.
rationale: Makes friction visible and reviewable; converts elimination recommendations into enforceable checks.
evidence: interactions.jsonl (90 steps; 62 recommend a change other than retain)

acceptance_criteria.given: a flow definition that renders a field with no Interaction Register entry
acceptance_criteria.then: the build fails naming the field and flow

acceptance_criteria.given: a register entry with basis 'convention' and no owner
acceptance_criteria.then: publication is rejected

acceptance_criteria.given: the donor wait step 'grant paid' with catalog event GrantPaymentSettled
acceptance_criteria.then: a notice is queued per the donor's preferences and the register shows the step as proactive

failure_conditions: Register drift from deployed flows
Basis mislabelled to avoid review
dependencies: RR-REQ-X-051-r1 contracts (uiField kind) supply field identities; UNB-RCN-PLT-002 catalog.
security_compliance: Necessity basis 'law' or 'security' entries require counsel or security owner sign-off; register contains no personal data.
ai_automation: AI may draft register entries from flow definitions (L2); a human owner approves.
ui_implications: Flows reference register IDs; fields with a default or inferred value render as prefilled review, not blank input.
api_implications: Embedded and API submissions validated against the same register so widgets cannot add questions.
testing_requirements: Build-time conformance test; synthetic journey fixtures per persona.
priority_justification: Prevents regression after simplification; not a launch blocker.
argue_for: Without enforcement, simplification decays as features add questions.
argue_against: Adds a governance artifact and build check.
existing_capability_alternative: Generate register from assistance contracts (RR-REQ-X-051-r1 uiField kind) rather than maintaining separately — preferred implementation.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Low-medium: register is generated; review effort only for convention-basis steps.
simplest_valid_alternative: Quarterly manual friction review — rejected because it does not prevent additions.
decision_rationale: Smallest enforceable mechanism that makes the principle testable.
open_questions: Should 'convention' steps carry an expiry forcing re-justification?
accessibility_considerations: Register records accessibility barrier per step so flows can be prioritised for assistive-technology testing.
expected_behavior: Unregistered inputs cannot ship; wait steps have notices.
exception_behavior: Emergency security step may ship with provisional entry valid 30 days [A].
adversarial_disposition: simplify to a design-review artefact plus CI check (SPF-ADV-018)

industry_analogy: n/a — internal analysis (comparable to outcome-driven setup wizards in SaaS; unverified — general knowledge)
why_no_predecessor: UNB-UI-S-023/S-054 cover activation and readiness checks, not how configuration values are obtained; XID-ADV-010 is a proposed decision.
business_problem: 110 configuration items are surfaced to a sponsor at onboarding; most have a correct default or are derivable.
statement: Sponsor onboarding MUST collect configuration through a versioned Outcome Questionnaire of at most 15 questions about the sponsor's legal identity, operating model, approval delegation, donor types, mission restrictions, money-in rails, grant payment methods, investment offering, fees, service model, brand and voice, risk appetite and statement cadence. Each answer MUST map, by a published deterministic derivation rule, to configuration items in the configuration register (UNB-SMP-CFG-003); every item not derived MUST take its policy-pack default (UNB-SMP-CFG-002). The resulting configuration MUST be presented as one reviewable draft with the derivation trace for each value, and MUST enter the normal policy lifecycle (draft, validate, simulate, approve). No item of disposition 'eliminate' or 'platform-owned' may be presented to the sponsor.
applicability: Every new tenant/legal sponsor; re-run on material operating-model change.
rationale: Ask about desired outcomes the sponsor can answer; derive the settings it cannot be expected to know.

acceptance_criteria.given: a sponsor answering Q2 'self-administered, Unbound keeps the books'
acceptance_criteria.then: BookOfRecord is Authoritative for all functions and FundsFlow is drafted from Q1 bank accounts, each with a trace to Q2

acceptance_criteria.given: a completed questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: no item with disposition eliminate or platform-owned appears, and the count of items requiring an explicit sponsor answer is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a derived value the sponsor edits
acceptance_criteria.when: the edit loosens a pack value
acceptance_criteria.then: it is rejected per UNB-SMP-CFG-002 with the pack rationale

failure_conditions: Derivation rule produces value outside pack bounds
Questionnaire answer ambiguous
dependencies: UNB-SMP-CFG-002 packs; UNB-SMP-CFG-003 register; RR-ADM-048-r1 simulation.
security_compliance: Answers stored as sponsor governance evidence; sponsor officer attests; platform staff hold A2 only (UNB-UI-S-023).
ai_automation: AI may explain questions and derived values from contracts (L0-L1) and prefill brand from public website (L2); it may not answer legal questions for the sponsor.
ui_implications: Readiness checklist shows questionnaire completion and derived-configuration approval as checks.
api_implications: Questionnaire and derivation rules exposed as assistance contracts.
reporting_implications: Onboarding metrics: questions answered, items overridden.
testing_requirements: Property test: every register item is either derived, pack-defaulted, eliminated or explicitly answered; golden fixtures per operating model.
priority_justification: Release-1 sponsor onboarding depends on default packs (XID-ADV-010).
argue_for: Turns a ~110-item onboarding into ~13 questions plus ~14 explicit values.
argue_against: Derivation rules are new logic to verify; wrong derivation could silently mis-configure.
existing_capability_alternative: Platform staff fill configuration for the sponsor — moves work rather than eliminating it.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Medium: derivation rules need golden fixtures per operating model.
customer_friction: Sponsor onboarding effort 288,000 s to 14,400 s for registers [A] (SPX-064).
simplest_valid_alternative: Single default pack with no questionnaire for release-1 reference sponsor — acceptable for R1 only.
decision_rationale: Retain sponsor control over the choices it legally owns; remove the rest from its view.
open_questions: Exact question wording requires sponsor user research (none exists).
preconditions: Contract executed; legal sponsor identity verified.
expected_behavior: Draft configuration with traces ready for approval.
exception_behavior: Unmappable answer routes to platform implementation specialist with case.

why_no_predecessor: XID-ADV-010 is a proposed decision; no requirement defines pack structure, override direction or upgrade behaviour.
business_problem: Per-sponsor authorship and counsel approval of ~20 registers is infeasible for small sponsors.
statement: Unbound MUST provide versioned Policy Packs, each a set of configuration item values with: pack ID and semantic version; reviewing authority (counsel, CPA, treasury) and review date per item; legal basis citation per item; default rationale; override direction per item (tightenOnly | lengthenOnly | sponsorChoice | none). A sponsor MUST adopt a pack version by an attestation command (A4, sponsor officer) that records attestor, pack hash and date. A sponsor override MUST be accepted only if it satisfies the item's override direction as evaluated by a deterministic comparator; any other override MUST be rejected unless approved through a recorded counsel deviation. When a new pack version is published, every attested sponsor MUST receive the diff, consequence simulation and effective date; adoption behaviour MUST follow SPD-CFG-001. Transactions and issued documents MUST pin the pack version in force.
applicability: All sponsor-configurable items with disposition default-in-pack or controlled-override.
rationale: Reviewed defaults satisfy most sponsors; tighten-only keeps protective floors.

acceptance_criteria.given: pack PK-TIMING sets destination cooling-off to 3 business days, tightenOnly
acceptance_criteria.then: the change is rejected with the pack rationale and legal basis

acceptance_criteria.given: a sponsor sets 5 business days
acceptance_criteria.then: it is accepted, recorded as an override and shown on the override metric (SPM-057)

acceptance_criteria.given: pack version 1.3 published while sponsor is attested to 1.2
acceptance_criteria.then: the sponsor receives the diff and simulation, and transactions continue pinning 1.2 until adoption per SPD-CFG-001

failure_conditions: Comparator mis-orders values (e.g. days vs business days)
Pack published without reviewer evidence

ai_automation: AI explains pack items from contracts; cannot author legal values.

api_implications: Pack and override exposed as assistance contracts with overrideDirection.
reporting_implications: Override count and pack currency metrics (SPM-057, SPM-058).
testing_requirements: Comparator property tests per value type; replay tests for pack upgrade.
argue_for: Removes per-sponsor legal authorship; preserves floors.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Medium-high: content maintenance across law changes; upgrade propagation.
customer_friction: Removes sponsor onboarding friction; none for donors.
simplest_valid_alternative: One pack per release with no overrides — too rigid for operating-model differences.
open_questions: Liability allocation (SPD-CFG-003)
Auto-apply vs re-attest (SPD-CFG-001)
financial_implications: Pack maintenance is a recurring platform cost; offsets per-sponsor counsel fees [A].
expected_behavior: Sponsors adopt by attestation; overrides only tighten.

why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-045 lists a configuration catalog but does not make settings justify cost or disposition.
business_problem: Configuration is a cost but is added as if free.
statement: Unbound MUST maintain a Configuration Register in which every sponsor- or platform-configurable item has: item ID; source requirement IDs; owner; who needs it and why; change frequency; default and whether it satisfies most sponsors; derivation rule if derivable; policy pack; conflicts; test and support cost (low | med | high); AI-assistance safety; disposition (eliminate | derive | default-in-pack | controlled-override | retain-configurable); and, for retain-configurable, the preserved reason (white-label, terminology, sponsor grant rules, affirmations, fees, operating-model difference). A new configurable item MUST NOT be merged unless its register entry exists and its disposition is approved by the product owner; items with disposition eliminate or platform-owned MUST NOT be exposed on sponsor surfaces or sponsor APIs.
rationale: Makes configuration cost explicit and reviewable.

acceptance_criteria.given: a pull request adding a sponsor-configurable parameter without register entry
acceptance_criteria.then: the build fails

acceptance_criteria.given: a register item with disposition platform-owned
acceptance_criteria.when: the sponsor configuration API schema is generated
acceptance_criteria.then: the item is absent

failure_conditions: Register not generated from code (drift)
ai_automation: AI may propose dispositions; human approves.
ui_implications: Sponsor configuration UI generated only from exposed items.
reporting_implications: Counts by disposition reported per release.
simplest_valid_alternative: Periodic manual audit — does not prevent additions.
expected_behavior: Every configurable item registered with disposition.

why_no_predecessor: REQ-X-049 and the work-queue specification name 'next best safe action' without ranking, evidence or authority rules; REQ-X-055 covers proactive detection, not ranking of interventions.
business_problem: Staff and customers need the one most valuable permitted action, not a dashboard to interpret.
statement: Every Next Best Action (NBA) shown on a dashboard, work queue or customer home MUST be generated from a registered Intervention type that declares: triggering condition (deterministic rule or metric threshold from the metric registry); evidence fields cited; expected outcome; ranking inputs (harm avoided or value protected, deadline proximity, legal clock, customer impact, effort) combined by a published deterministic ranking rule; the domain command it opens and that command's authority class (UNB-RCN-PLT-005). An NBA MUST be shown as actionable only if the viewer currently holds authority for the command; otherwise it MUST be shown as unavailable with the reason and the role that can act. Selecting an NBA MUST open the authoritative command with re-checked state and MUST NOT execute A3 or higher actions directly. AI MAY explain or draft evidence for an NBA but MUST NOT change its rank.
applicability: Staff work surfaces, sponsor overview, donor/advisor/charity homes ('Needs your attention').
rationale: Converts metrics into permitted, evidence-backed actions while preserving authority boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.given: an aged provider-Unknown payment and a treasury analyst without release authority
acceptance_criteria.then: the NBA 'Query provider status' is actionable and 'Reissue payment' is never proposed (RR-REQ-X-004-r1)

acceptance_criteria.given: a grant approval NBA for a grants officer whose delegation expired
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows unavailable with reason 'delegation expired' and the role that can act

acceptance_criteria.given: two NBAs with equal harm but different legal deadlines
acceptance_criteria.then: the earlier legal deadline ranks first and the rank explanation cites both inputs

failure_conditions: Ranking rule not reproducible
NBA executes without recheck
security_compliance: Authority evaluated server-side at render and at command; no information leakage about records outside scope.
ui_implications: One primary action per task (UNB-UI-DS-009); unavailable-action pattern (FORMA-GAP-11).
api_implications: NBA feed API returns intervention type, rank inputs, command reference.
reporting_implications: NBA acceptance, dismissal and outcome tracked to validate ranking.
testing_requirements: Ranking golden fixtures; authority matrix property tests.
priority_justification: Improves staff and customer effectiveness; R1 can use rule-ordered task lists.
argue_for: Prevents dashboards that inform but do not direct.
existing_capability_alternative: Sort by SLA risk (UNB-UI-S-008) — acceptable fallback.
customer_friction: Reduces: donors see one clear next step.
decision_rationale: Formalise what is already implied, with authority limits.
open_questions: Weights for harm vs deadline require operations owner approval.
accessibility_considerations: Rank explanation in text; not colour-coded only.
preconditions: Metric registry and authority matrix exist.
exception_behavior: If ranking inputs missing, fall back to SLA-risk sort and flag.

discovery_source: Phase 12 architecture re-evaluation under the minimum-touch operating model (this group, eval)
why_no_predecessor: UNB-CUST-022 covers custodian outages only; UNB-XIN-SAS-002 kill switches stop new commands but define no capacity-aware fallback; RR-REQ-X-007-r1 holds on stale data but does not bound or project the backlog.
business_problem: When an automated decision path is suspended (stale source, rule suspended, kill switch), work either floods a small human team or is released unsafely.
statement: Each automated decision path (policy grant approval, charity status refresh, automated reconciliation matching, automated contribution acceptance) MUST declare a fallback mode of Hold or HumanQueue and an expected human minutes per item. When the path is suspended or its inputs are stale, the system MUST apply the declared fallback, MUST notify affected donors/advisors/charities with a reason class and an expected next-update time, and MUST compute and display the projected backlog clearance time against the rostered capacity for the reviewing role. The system MUST NOT release, approve or match any held item solely because of its age or backlog size.
applicability: All sponsors; all automated decision paths.
rationale: Minimum-touch removes the human slack that degraded modes implicitly relied on (SPF-ARX-004).

acceptance_criteria.given: Tier-1 policy approval suspended because the IRS status source is older than the freshness window on a December day with 8,000 recommendations
acceptance_criteria.then: each is held with reason SourceStale, donors see the reason class and next-update time, and the backlog projection shows clearance time against the rostered reviewers

acceptance_criteria.given: a HumanQueue fallback with 300 items older than the SLA
acceptance_criteria.then: no item is approved or released; an escalation case opens for the sponsor operations owner

acceptance_criteria.given: an automated path without a declared fallback mode
acceptance_criteria.then: enablement is rejected

failure_conditions: any held item auto-released by age
fallback undeclared for an enabled path
backlog projection missing during suspension
dependencies: Roster model (UNB-SMP-CLR-001) for capacity; freshness watermarks (UNB-XIN-EVA-004).
security_compliance: Fallback cannot bypass holds or approvals; notices must not disclose sanctions or investigation reasons (reason classes only).
ai_automation: Applies to every automated path; AI cannot clear held items.
ui_implications: Operations exception surface shows suspension state, backlog and projection; donor/charity status shows reason class.
api_implications: Status endpoints expose reason class and expected update time; partner events expose only partner-safe states (UNB-XIN-EVA-008).
reporting_implications: Suspension minutes and backlog peaks reported monthly.
testing_requirements: Property test: no transition from Held to Released without a fresh evaluation; simulation TB-10.
priority_justification: Required before enabling Tier-1 approval at volume; not a launch blocker for manual-first operation.
argue_for: Prevents unsafe auto-release and makes fallback cost visible.
argue_against: Adds a per-path declaration and a projection feature.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Small: one declaration table, one projection query, notification templates.
customer_friction: Holds are visible and explained instead of silent delays.
simplest_valid_alternative: Hold-only fallback for every path with a static message; projection added later.
decision_rationale: Hold-and-notify is the only fallback a small team can sustain at December volume.
open_questions: What donor-visible SLA is acceptable during suspension?
Which paths may use HumanQueue at all?
accessibility_considerations: Notices in accessible formats; status not conveyed by colour alone.
financial_implications: No money moves while held; no fee changes.
expected_behavior: Declared fallback applied; notifications and projection produced.
exception_behavior: If roster data unavailable, projection shows Unknown and escalation opens.

discovery_source: Phase 11 Clarity evaluation of R8 (this group, eval)
parent_capability: Organization, segregation of duties, delegation of authority
why_no_predecessor: No requirement models a roster; the organization model and the operations review both call for one (review-fin-ops B-2) and none exists.
business_problem: Staffing targets are stated as headcount against an undefined floor; SoD coverage on worst days is untested.
statement: The platform MUST maintain a roster of authorized workforce principals per sponsor by role and calendar day (including holidays and declared absences) and MUST compute, for each SoD-constrained command class, whether at least two eligible, mutually independent principals are available on each day of a forward horizon of at least 30 days. A day with fewer than two eligible principals for any SoD-constrained role MUST be reported as a coverage gap to the sponsor operations owner. During a gap, commands requiring the uncovered role MUST be held rather than executed under an SoD waiver.
rationale: Turns "staffing floor" into a testable coverage property (Clarity: Systems Over Heroes; operational test).

acceptance_criteria.given: a roster where only one eligible reconciler independent of the releaser is available on Dec 26
acceptance_criteria.then: Dec 26 is reported as a coverage gap for the reconciler role

acceptance_criteria.given: a coverage gap for the payee-profile approver role today
acceptance_criteria.then: it is held with reason RoleUncovered and no SoD waiver path is offered

acceptance_criteria.given: a pre-authorized outsourced principal named in the DoA for the role
acceptance_criteria.then: that principal counts toward coverage only within the delegation scope and dates

failure_conditions: gap not detected
command executed under waiver during a gap
outsourced principal counted outside delegation
dependencies: Workforce feed (UNB-XIN-ERP-005 already references it); DoA entries.
security_compliance: Roster is an authority fact owned by IAM; changes audited.
ui_implications: Coverage calendar on the operations surface.
reporting_implications: Monthly coverage-gap report to sponsor board.
testing_requirements: Property test over random rosters: no SoD-constrained command executes on a day with < 2 eligible independent principals.
priority_justification: Needed before any staffing target is set; SoD controls are P0 elsewhere.
argue_for: Replaces an unresolved number with a checkable property.
argue_against: Workforce scheduling is adjacent to HR (explicitly not built, report 10).
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Moderate: roster input and a coverage query; not an HR system.
customer_friction: Holds during gaps delay donors; preferable to waivers.
simplest_valid_alternative: Import a rota file and compute coverage; no scheduling UI.
decision_rationale: Only form in which R8 can be evaluated.
open_questions: Which roles may be held by outsourced principals?
Is two-deep the right independence depth for every role?
accessibility_considerations: Calendar views keyboard-navigable and screen-reader labelled.
financial_implications: Avoids SoD waivers on money movement.
expected_behavior: Coverage computed daily; gaps reported; uncovered commands held.
exception_behavior: If workforce feed stale, coverage reported Unknown and treated as a gap.

discovery_source: Phase 11 Clarity/EDF evaluation of R7 (this group, eval)
why_no_predecessor: Report 16 gates five features on opinions; no requirement ties every policy-pack element or rule version to the confirmation status of the decision that justifies it.
business_problem: Provisional legal/accounting positions can reach production through packs and rules without confirmation.
statement: Every policy-pack element, rule version and accounting-treatment setting MUST record the decision identifiers it relies on and each decision's basis status (provisional, confirmed, superseded). A version whose basis includes any provisional decision MUST NOT be activated in a production sponsor environment. When a decision is superseded, the system MUST list every active version, sponsor and record class that relies on it and MUST open a change case for each.
applicability: All sponsors; all policy packs, rules and accounting settings.
rationale: Stops Assumption Drift at the irreversible boundary (Clarity correctability; EDF control point CP1 for R7).

acceptance_criteria.given: a recognition-point pack element relying on XID-ADV-006 with status provisional
acceptance_criteria.when: activation in a production sponsor is attempted
acceptance_criteria.then: activation is rejected with reason ProvisionalBasis and the decision id

acceptance_criteria.given: XID-BNK-006 superseded after counsel review
acceptance_criteria.then: every active version relying on it is listed with affected sponsors and a change case is opened for each

acceptance_criteria.given: the same element in a synthetic-data environment
acceptance_criteria.then: activation succeeds and the environment is labelled non-production

failure_conditions: provisional-basis version active in production
supersession without impact listing
security_compliance: Basis status changes require an authorized counsel/CPA principal.
ai_automation: AI may draft but not change basis status.
ui_implications: Basis badge on every pack element.
reporting_implications: Count of provisional-basis elements by sponsor on the launch-readiness report.
testing_requirements: Property: no production activation with a provisional dependency.
priority_justification: Prevents unconfirmed legal/accounting positions from producing irreversible external effects.
argue_for: Cheap, deterministic, closes a real propagation path.
argue_against: May block launch if confirmations lag.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Low: a dependency field and a check.
simplest_valid_alternative: Launch checklist listing provisional decisions per feature.
decision_rationale: Machine enforcement survives staff turnover and pressure (Clarity operational test).
open_questions: Which decisions are "basis" for which elements (mapping effort)?
exception_behavior: If register unavailable, activation fails closed.

industry_analogy: Trust companies: a named trust officer acts for each trust; bank dual control
parent_capability: Authority matrix and delegation of authority
why_no_predecessor: UNB-XIN-CLM-008 bars vendor staff without appointment from A3+, and UNB-XIN-ERP-005 keeps the DoA register, but nothing forbids one person holding A3+ authority for several sponsors, nothing records which organization employs a principal, and nothing anticipates administrators acting for several sponsors.
business_problem: Sponsors hold exclusive legal control. Unbound supplies software only, so every decider must be the sponsor's own; customers that administer several sponsors must never become a shared decision team. Unbound may later offer staffed services, which must not need a re-design.
statement: Every principal MUST be recorded with an employing Organization of type Sponsor, Administrator or Vendor, and with the sponsors each Administrator is contracted to act for. A delegation-of-authority entry at level A3 or above for a sponsor (UNB-XIN-ERP-005; UNB-RCN-PLT-005) MUST be refused unless the principal belongs to that sponsor's DecisionTeam and holds no active A3+ entry for any other sponsor. In release 1 a DecisionTeam member MUST be employed or board-appointed by that sponsor: principals of Administrator or Vendor organizations MUST NOT hold A3+ authority. Administrator principals MAY perform non-reserved work (service, operations, evidence assembly, case preparation) for the sponsors they are contracted for; Vendor principals MAY perform only platform support under the access controls. Reserved work items MUST be routed only to the owning sponsor's DecisionTeam; no queue, assignment pool, delegate list or AI agent may route a reserved item to anyone else. Each sponsor MUST carry a StaffingModel value; only SponsorStaffed is enabled. The values OperatorDedicated and AffiliatedSponsor MUST exist in the schema but stay disabled, and enabling one MUST require a recorded owner decision and a release flag, without schema change.
applicability: All sponsors on a shared platform; a self-operated sponsor satisfies it trivially.
rationale: Implements both decisions as invariants at the DoA register and the router, and leaves typed hooks for later operator services.

acceptance_criteria.given: Principal P holds an active A4 entry for sponsor S1
acceptance_criteria.when: an A3 entry for P at sponsor S2 is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused with reason CrossSponsorAuthority and an audit event; S1's entry is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: Administrator AD is contracted for S1 and S2; principal Q is employed by AD
acceptance_criteria.when: an A3 entry for Q at S1 is submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: it is refused with reason NotSponsorDecider; Q can still assemble evidence for S1 and S2 cases

acceptance_criteria.given: S1's whole DecisionTeam is absent
acceptance_criteria.when: an S1 exception grant reaches the reserved queue
acceptance_criteria.then: it is not offered to AD or S2 principals; it waits and a CoverageGap item opens (UNB-SMP-ORG-002)

acceptance_criteria.given: The release flag for OperatorDedicated is off
acceptance_criteria.when: an administrator sets S1's StaffingModel to OperatorDedicated
acceptance_criteria.then: the change is refused; with the flag on and an owner decision recorded it is accepted without a schema migration

failure_conditions: Two sponsors' reserved items reachable from one assignment pool
Administrator or Vendor principal holding A3+ authority
A disabled StaffingModel usable through the API
Adding a staffing model later requires a schema change
dependencies: DoA register keyed by principal across sponsors
Organization and contract records for administrators
Router aware of reserved decision classes
security_compliance: Cross-sponsor uniqueness check needs a platform-wide principal identity; each sponsor sees only pass/fail, not another sponsor's roster. Vendor support access is logged and time-bound.
ai_automation: Deterministic checks. AI may prepare dossiers for administrators but never decides and never routes reserved items across sponsors.
ui_implications: Sponsor settings show the DecisionTeam roster and StaffingModel; disabled models are not offered. Refusals explain the reason without naming other sponsors.
api_implications: DoA commands return CrossSponsorAuthority or NotSponsorDecider; StaffingModel accepts only enabled values; routing refuses cross-sponsor reserved assignment.
reporting_implications: Per-sponsor roster and coverage; administrator activity by sponsor; audit report of refused entries.
testing_requirements: Property test: every reserved item's assignee belongs to the item's sponsor's DecisionTeam; fixtures for administrators, end-dated entries and flag toggling.
priority_justification: Owner decision on sponsor legal control; every platform cost figure depends on it.
argue_for: Clear accountability per sponsor; no conflicts between sponsors; matches exclusive legal control.
argue_against: Each sponsor carries a minimum team; small sponsors become expensive to run (SPF-ECN-015).
existing_capability_alternative: UNB-XIN-CLM-008 covers appointment, not exclusivity across sponsors.
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Low to moderate in software: organization and contract records, two refusal rules, an enumerated staffing model with flags.
customer_friction: None for donors; sponsors must name their team before go-live.
simplest_valid_alternative: Contractual promise without a system check (rejected: not testable).
open_questions: Whether a principal may move from one sponsor's team to another's without a waiting period (default: no overlap only).
Appointment form if OperatorDedicated is ever enabled (SPD-ORG-002).

Minimum time share per DecisionTeam holder when an administrator does the non-reserved work. Report 24 assumes 0.5 FTE each (2.5 FTE in total); the value decides whether the administrator route is cheaper than sponsor-direct.
accessibility_considerations: Roster and rejection messages available as text tables.
financial_implications: Sets each sponsor's minimum decision staff, borne by the sponsor (report 24).
preconditions: Platform-wide principal identity; DoA register; organization records.
expected_behavior: Only a sponsor's own people decide for that sponsor; administrators prepare; Unbound supports the software.
exception_behavior: If the uniqueness check is unavailable, A3+ entry activation is held, not allowed.

industry_analogy: SaaS licensing: per-seat or per-unit fee plus per-tenant fee, with add-on service lines
why_no_predecessor: UNB-XIN-ECO-012 and UNB-XIN-SAS-009 price per account; no record prices a sponsor tenant, bills an administrator for several sponsors, or allows service components to be added later.
business_problem: Unbound sells software. Per-sponsor platform cost (tenant set-up, authority-register set-up, support) cannot be recovered fairly by a per-account fee alone, and Unbound may later sell staffed services.
statement: Unbound's charges SHALL be computed from a typed list of fee components. In release 1 only two types are enabled: (A) a per-account licence fee by ServicingClass and (B) a per-sponsor annual tenant fee. Quotes, invoices and cost-to-serve reports SHALL itemize A and B for each sponsor, including when an Administrator is billed for several sponsors. Adding a new component type later (for example operator-supplied staffing under SPR-ADV-009) SHALL require only configuration and a recorded owner decision, and SHALL NOT change any existing customer's charges until their contract is amended. Fee components and amounts SHALL NOT be inputs to eligibility, sanctions, approval, grant priority or payment timing.
rationale: Licence pricing that matches a software-only business, with a hook for services.

acceptance_criteria.given: Administrator AD acts for sponsors S1 (5,000 accounts) and S2 (20,000 accounts)
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows A and B separately for S1 and for S2, and the totals equal the sum of the lines

acceptance_criteria.given: A new component type 'OperatorStaffing' is configured but no owner decision is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the component is not offered; once the decision is recorded it can be added to new contracts only

acceptance_criteria.given: Two sponsors differ only in licence tier
acceptance_criteria.when: the same exception grant is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.then: eligibility, approval path and payment timing are identical

failure_conditions: Per-sponsor cost hidden in the per-account fee
Administrator invoice not itemized by sponsor
A new component type changing existing contracts
Fee tier influencing grant handling
security_compliance: Commercial terms visible to Unbound finance staff and the billed customer only.
ai_automation: Deterministic fee computation; AI may draft invoice explanations only.
ui_implications: Quote shows A and B per sponsor; future component types are hidden until enabled.
api_implications: Quote and invoice APIs return typed components per sponsor.
reporting_implications: Revenue and vendor cost per sponsor and per component.
testing_requirements: Invoice fixtures for a direct sponsor and an administrator with several sponsors; test that enabling a component type leaves existing contracts unchanged.
priority_justification: Needed before the first customer contract.
argue_for: Simple software pricing now; services can be added later without re-design.
argue_against: A tenant fee makes very small sponsors pay a visible minimum.
existing_capability_alternative: UNB-XIN-ECO-012 per-account pricing (no tenant fee, no administrator billing).
cost_and_hidden_complexity: Low to moderate: component catalogue and per-sponsor itemization.
customer_friction: None for donors; administrators get one invoice itemized by sponsor.
simplest_valid_alternative: Single per-account fee with a minimum (rejected: hides per-sponsor cost and has no service hook).
open_questions: Price levels and margin for A and B (CFO + commercial lead).
Whether B scales with sponsor size.
accessibility_considerations: Quote comparison available as an accessible table.
financial_implications: Recovers Unbound's software cost: about $11 per account plus $52,000 per sponsor at OM3@1M before margin (report 24).
expected_behavior: Customers pay a licence; each sponsor's charges are visible separately.
exception_behavior: If a component cannot be computed, the invoice is held, not estimated.
